title: Cleft Sentences
theory:
 A cleft sentence is a sentence divided into two parts to emphasize a particular element
 (subject, object, time, place, etc.).

 Structures
 1 It-cleft structure: It + be (is/was) + emphasized part + that/who + rest of the sentence
 2 Wh-cleft (Pseudo-cleft) structure: Wh-word (what/where/why etc.) + clause + be +
 emphasized part
 Note
  When a noun clause performs the function of the subject of a verb, a singular verb is
 used. Noun Clause as subject usually begins with (that, what, who, whoever, whether,
 how, etc).
